item.title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network material models can represent yield surfaces and hardening laws with far more flexibility than classical closed-form plasticity formulations, but training such a model end-to-end through an implicit return map introduces non-trivial challenges. This work presents a thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive model for rate-independent, isotropic elastoplasticity that jointly learns a flexible yield function together with its evolution laws. For non-associative flow, the yield function extends the convex flow potential by a jointly trained additive term, which renders the model thermodynamically consistent by construction. Isotropy and convexity are enforced simultaneously across all learnable components through a permutation-invariant, spectral (eigenvalue-based) representation. Training proceeds through a backward-Euler return map, with gradients propagated by the implicit function theorem together with an eigenvalue-degeneracy-aware scheme for safe differentiation. The robustness and generality of the approach are demonstrated by reproducing known constitutive models, including non-associative flow, learning material behavior from stress--strain data extracted from a full-field finite element simulation, and capturing unknown non-associative behavior from homogenized representative volume elements of a foam. Finally, the proposed neural plasticity model is evaluated within finite element simulations to solve boundary-value-problem under plane stress.
item.dc:creator: Harikrishnan Vijayakumaran, Shunyu Yin, Martin Abendroth, Miguel A. Bessa, Karl A. Kalina

item.title: N -phase flow simulations using X-Mesh and an explicit marker interface representation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a marker-based X-Mesh framework for incompressible N-phase flow simulations with sharp, explicitly tracked interfaces. The interface is represented by Lagrangian marker chains, while the computational mesh is deformed so that selected mesh edges conform to the tracked geometry without changing mesh connectivity. This combination preserves the advantages of body-fitted finite element discretizations while allowing highly distorted and nearly degenerated elements to capture fine interfacial features on relatively coarse meshes without requiring mesh refinement. The arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) finite element solver uses a pressure field that is continuous within each phase and discontinuous across the fitted interface. Surface tension is introduced through a variational membrane, so the pressure jump is resolved without prescribing a curvature-dependent correction; a Young wall energy provides the corresponding treatment of fluid-fluid-solid triple points. Topological changes are handled geometrically from the marker representation. Numerical experiments illustrate the ability of the approach to transport complex interfaces and to control topology changes through marker-based feature-size criteria.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Quiriny, Jonathan Lambrechts, Michel Henry, Nicolas Mo\"es, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Remacle

item.title: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural operators (NOs) have been introduced as deep learning-powered solutions to the computational bottleneck of solving families of problems. Once trained, an NO can rapidly output approximate solutions, avoiding the need to rerun classical solvers. However, standard NO architectures cannot guarantee static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces from market or model features and, as we verify experimentally, can yield negative PnL in downstream trading tasks. We introduce a certifiably arbitrage-free (AF) and universal encoder-decoder NO framework, continuously mapping inputs from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) $\mathcal{H}$ over any fixed subset of $[0,\infty)^2$ to a convex combination of arbitrage-free European call-price surfaces by continuously solving an approximate nearest-neighbour problem. We show that a nearest arbitrage-free correction of an unconstrained predicted surface need not exist, implying that no-arbitrage cannot, in general, be restored through post-processing. Further, we show that standard NOs, such as the FNO and certain encoder-decoder NOs, admit parameter configurations whose outputs violate static no-arbitrage. Thus, out-of-the-box NOs generally cannot be certifiably restricted to arbitrage-free configurations, but may only be guided towards them through PINN-type regularization during training.
item.dc:creator: Anastasis Kratsios, Yannick Limmer, Hans Buehler, Blanka Horvath, Raeid Saqur

item.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
item.description: arXiv:2611.13161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3 times, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20-30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts immediately to human verbal updates. Ablation studies confirm that both the shared cognitive workspace and language grounding are critical to overall system performance. Overall, this work establishes a new paradigm for language-guided multi-agent SAR robotics, demonstrating that semantic grounding combined with hierarchical reasoning enables safer, more efficient, and more interpretable autonomous rescue operations.
item.dc:creator: Sepideh Ravanbakhsh, Hamidreza Moradi

item.title: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Much of the variation in financial time series is driven by market-wide shocks that cannot be predicted from an asset's own history. Per-asset self-supervised learning treats this variation as irreducible noise. Under a latent factor model, we show that conditioning prediction on the realized market factor makes the asset's market exposure necessary for optimal prediction, while reducing the noise against which the asset-specific component is learned. Building on this insight, we introduce Market-Conditioned JEPA (MC-JEPA), a joint-embedding predictive architecture for financial time series. During training, we construct a leave-one-out market condition for each asset from the future target embeddings of other assets and incorporate it through factor loadings derived from the asset's own representation. On 11 years of minute-level Chinese A-share data, MC-JEPA improves over per-asset JEPA across nine targets spanning returns, market exposure, risk, and liquidity, with the strongest and most statistically significant gains in exposure, risk, and liquidity. It achieves the best RankIC on all liquidity targets and on return horizons from two hours to five days, outperforming time-series foundation models and self-supervised baselines, and delivers the best portfolio performance in a historical backtest. Ablations show that the return and exposure gains require the condition to be aligned with the realized market movement. After restoring the volatility scale removed by normalization, the predictor's factor loadings rank stocks by market beta nearly as well as a supervised probe, without labels. A synthetic factor-model study with known parameters shows that conditioning improves the recovery of both market exposure and the asset-specific component.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Wang, Fengyuan Liu, Mukai Li, Haochen Luo, Lei Li, Qi Liu

item.title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
item.description: arXiv:2611.14158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational homogenization and coupled multiscale simulations of heterogeneous materials require repeated solution of mechanical fields on Representative Volume Elements, which becomes prohibitively expensive for high-resolution three-dimensional microstructures. Machine-learning surrogates can accelerate these computations, yet most existing approaches predict fields for fixed macroscopic loadings and provide limited guidance on how to scale network architectures for high-resolution 3D tensor-field prediction. This work presents a U-Net surrogate trained to predict the full 36-component strain localization tensor field in voxelized concrete mesostructures at resolutions up to $256^3$. Training localization tensors are generated with an FFT-based linear elastic solver, and an extensive hyperparameter optimization is performed to derive scaling rules and an accuracy-speed trade-off analysis. The results show that only network width and depth need to be scaled with problem complexity, while several conventional U-Net design choices, such as doubling channels after downsampling, are suboptimal for this problem. The final neural network achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 1.118% on both the validation and the held-out test sets, and an inference speedup of approximately 8.7x over the FFT-based solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU. Generalization experiments reveal transfer across aggregate volume fractions and highlight the importance of training on diverse morphologies. To safeguard reliability, a Maximum Mean Discrepancy metric computed on internal feature maps is proposed for detecting out-of-distribution microstructures without costly reference computations.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Fourel, Paul Devianne, Marine Debouvry, Tristan Destruhaut, Russell Gunn, Ashwini Gupta, Lori Graham-Brady, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Molinari

item.title: A unifying view of contrastive learning, importance sampling, and bridge sampling for energy-based models
item.description: arXiv:2604.08116v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the last decades, energy-based models (EBMs) have become an important class of probabilistic models in which a component of the likelihood is intractable and therefore cannot be evaluated explicitly. Consequently, parameter estimation in EBMs is challenging for conventional inference methods. This work is a review paper that brings together these different methodological contributions within a unified framework, highlighting the connections among noise contrastive estimation (NCE), reverse logistic regression (RLR), Bennett's acceptance-ratio (BAR) method, multiple importance sampling (MIS), and bridge sampling within the context of EBMs. Some of them are equivalent under specific conditions. This unified perspective clarifies relationships among existing methods and enables the development of new estimators, with the potential to improve statistical and computational efficiency. Furthermore, this study helps elucidate the success of NCE in terms of its flexibility and robustness, while also identifying scenarios in which its performance can be further improved. Our aim is to provide a self-contained and accessible treatment, with clear and straightforward derivations, that brings together these contributions within a common framework and makes the main results and their underlying ideas understandable to a broader readership. The contribution is twofold. First, this work serves as a comprehensive tutorial for researchers entering the field, introducing the fundamental concepts and derivations. Second, it offers a thorough review for experienced practitioners. The code used in the numerical experiments is available to support the reproducibility of the results.
item.dc:creator: Luca Martino

item.title: DREChanNet: Patient-Relative iEEG Model for Channel-Wise Epileptogenic Zone Localization
item.description: arXiv:2608.01076v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate localization of the epileptogenic zone (EZ) is essential for presurgical evaluation of patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) provides direct recordings of seizure-related brain activity, yet identifying epileptogenic contacts remains challenging because background electrophysiological activity and electrode coverage vary substantially across patients. These differences complicate the interpretation of absolute signal measurements and highlight the need to account for patient-specific recording context. We propose a patient-relative (PR) plug-in that expresses physiological features or learned representations relative to the distribution of recorded channels within each patient. This label-free operation can be incorporated as an input transformation or a lightweight correction to an existing predictor. We further introduce DREChanNet, a compact ictal localization model integrating six physiological descriptors with learned raw-signal representations. Same-channel pre-onset contrasts characterize seizure-related changes, cross-seizure aggregation preserves response magnitude and variability, and PR contextualizes both branches before prediction. We investigate within-patient physiological associations and held-out-channel reference prediction, followed by baseline comparisons, component ablations, cross-source transfer, seizure-sufficiency analysis, and channel ranking. Evaluation includes an ictal cohort of 80 patients and a patient-based interictal cohort of 124 patients. PR improves macro-F1 by an average of 9.03 percentage points across eight ictal baselines and improves the separately fitted interictal readout. These findings support patient-relative contextualization as a reusable approach to channel-level localization and establish DREChanNet as an integrated model for ictal iEEG analysis.
item.dc:creator: Yuanchu Gong, Zibo Yan, Yibo Lyu, Zhe Shi, Qiang Li, Yuanfeng Zhou, Minqiang Yang, Yalin Wang, Wei Chen, Bin Hu

item.title: MC$^2$: Monte Carlo Correction for Fast Elliptic PDE Solving
item.description: arXiv:2605.09288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Partial differential equation (PDE) solvers underpin modern computer graphics, geometry processing, and scientific computing. Classical Monte Carlo PDE solvers such as Walk-on-Spheres (WoS) provide mesh-free estimations that are unbiased, but with accuracy limited by sampling and numerical approximation. Learned solvers are fast but biased and brittle under distribution shift. We therefore present MC$^2$, a hybrid Neural Network-Monte Carlo PDE solver that treats a low-budget Monte Carlo solution as a structured estimator of the true field and learns a single-pass neural correction to recover a high-fidelity solution. MC$^2$ matches the accuracy of solutions using over $1000\times$ more Monte Carlo samples, outperforming all evaluated mesh-free classical, denoising, and neural-operator baselines. To enable reproducible study of finite-compute PDE solving, we additionally release PDEZoo, the largest standardized elliptic PDE benchmark to date: 2 million PDEs spanning 5 elliptic families and unlimited geometric compositions, with analytic ground truth and multi-budget Monte Carlo trajectories. Together, MC$^2$ and PDEZoo (1) empirically establish that finite-sample Monte Carlo error is structured, learnable, and correctable in a single forward pass, (2) show that we can solve PDEs $\sim$218$\times$ faster than WoS at matched accuracy and achieve a $\sim$171$\times$ reduction in inference time relative to state-of-the-art diffusion methods while attaining higher accuracy, and (3) provide the reproducible evaluation infrastructure the field has so far lacked. Code & Data: https://mc-error-correction.github.io
item.dc:creator: Ethan Hsu, Hong Meng Yam, Ivan Ge

item.title: Shape optimisation of nonlinear Naghdi shells on discrete geometries
item.description: arXiv:2608.10342v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an automated framework for the shape optimisation of a geometrically nonlinear, five-parameter Naghdi model on faceted triangulations. By recovering directors numerically, we remove the requirement for an analytic or spline parameterisation of the mid-surface, whereas partial selective reduced integration alleviates locking. The residual and tangent of symbolic energies are generated in an automated fashion building on Firedrake's and UFL's symbolic differentiation capabilities. Additionally, UFL's and pyadjoint's algorithmic differentiation enables automated first and second shape derivative evaluations that are verifiably correct via Taylor tests. The forward model agrees with the Sze/Abaqus semi-cylinder reference. A three-model mesh-refinement study indicates that geometry recovery and surface faceting have small effects on the predicted deflection. Numerical experiments show that 100 trust-region iterations suffice to reduce the squared-displacement functional of a semi-cylinder by 98.4% and the elastic strain energy of a bracket by 94.6%. The latter result is validated against a COMSOL benchmark. Non-uniqueness of optimal shapes is demonstrated by optimising initial designs subject to small perturbations. Comparisons with linearised designs distinguish optimisation performance from the accuracy of the predicted nonlinear response.
item.dc:creator: Ado Farsi, Alberto Paganini
